source: Department of Agricultural Extension (នាយកដ្ឋានផ្សព្វផ្សាយកសិកម្ម), Ministry of Agriculture, Forestry and Fisheries, Cambodia — booklet 'ដំណាំពោត' (Corn Crop), Issue 1, 2003, funded by Asian Development Bank (ADB), Loan/Grant No. 1445-CAM(SF), section IV.1-2: Seed selection and planting season
text:
Seed selection criteria for corn: seed should be full/plump, not shriveled; seed should have purity of at least 95%; seed should have a germination rate of at least 85%; seed should be fresh, not stored/exposed for more than 2 years; and seed should be free of insect and disease damage, whole and unbroken.

Planting season: In areas where planting does not depend on a fixed season, farmers in Cambodia can grow corn along a number of provinces situated along the river, such as Kandal, Prey Veng, Kampong Cham, Kratie, Kampong Thom, and red-soil growing areas. For land along riverbanks specifically, farmers can plant 2 crops per year because water and soil fertility are sufficiently available there.

Rainy-season crop: planting begins in April through mid-May, with harvest in August, particularly on riverbank land.

Dry (receding-water) season crop: planting begins from November through January, with harvest from late March into early April, particularly on riverbank land.
